creators.name: Sol LeWitt
creators.bio: American artist (1928–2007) central to Minimal and Conceptual art. His wall drawings exist as written instructions that assistants and institutions execute again and again.
creators.why: He wrote the founding statements that treat the artwork as an idea that others carry out, the direct ancestor of protocol art.
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家（1928–2007），极简主义与观念艺术的核心人物。他的墙绘以书面指令的形式存在，由助手和机构一次次执行。
creators.why_zh: 他写下了把作品视为交由他人执行之观念的奠基性文字，是协议艺术的直接前身。

creators.name: Jack Burnham
creators.bio: American artist and critic (1931–2019) who brought systems theory and cybernetics into art criticism in Artforum and curated the 1970 exhibition Software at the Jewish Museum.
creators.why: He argued that art was moving from objects to systems of relations between people, machines and institutions.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、评论家与策展人
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家与评论家（1931–2019），在《Artforum》上把系统论和控制论引入艺术批评，并于 1970 年在犹太博物馆策划展览 Software。
creators.why_zh: 他提出艺术正从物体转向由人、机器和机构之间关系构成的系统。

creators.name: Roy Ascott
creators.role: Artist and theorist of telematic art
creators.bio: British artist and educator (born 1934) who developed cybernetic art teaching in the 1960s and telematic network artworks from the late 1970s.
creators.why: He framed networked art as distributed authorship, where meaning is made by many participants connected through a network.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、远程通信艺术理论家
creators.bio_zh: 英国艺术家与教育者（1934 年生），1960 年代发展出控制论式的艺术教学，1970 年代末起创作远程通信网络作品。
creators.why_zh: 他把网络艺术阐释为分布式创作：意义由通过网络相连的众多参与者共同生成。

creators.name: Benjamin H. D. Buchloh
creators.bio: German art historian (born 1941) and editor of October, known for his histories of Conceptual art and postwar European art.
creators.why: He described Conceptual art as an 'aesthetic of administration': art made of certificates, lists, contracts and bureaucratic procedures.
creators.bio_zh: 德国艺术史学者（1941 年生），《October》编辑，以观念艺术和战后欧洲艺术研究著称。
creators.why_zh: 他把观念艺术描述为一种“管理美学”：由证书、清单、契约和官僚程序构成的艺术。

creators.name: Alexander R. Galloway
creators.bio: American media theorist at New York University and a founding member of the software art collective RSG (Radical Software Group).
creators.why: His book Protocol gave art and media theory its working definition of protocol as the form control takes in decentralized networks.
creators.bio_zh: 美国媒介理论家，任教于纽约大学，软件艺术团体 RSG（Radical Software Group）的创始成员。
creators.why_zh: 他的《Protocol》一书为艺术与媒介理论提供了“协议”的基本定义：协议是控制在去中心化网络中的存在形式。

creators.name: Eugene Thacker
creators.bio: American philosopher and writer, professor at The New School, who has written on biotechnology, networks and the philosophy of horror.
creators.why: With Galloway he wrote The Exploit, a theory of how networks are controlled and how they can be resisted from inside their protocols.
creators.bio_zh: 美国哲学家与作家，任教于新学院（The New School），著述涉及生物技术、网络与恐怖哲学。
creators.why_zh: 他与 Galloway 合著《The Exploit》，讨论网络如何被控制，以及如何从协议内部进行抵抗。

creators.name: Florian Cramer
creators.role: Writer and researcher on code and culture
creators.bio: German writer and researcher on literature, computing and media culture, long associated with the Piet Zwart Institute and Willem de Kooning Academy in Rotterdam.
creators.why: He traced the idea of executable instructions from magic formulas and combinatory poetry to software, linking scores to code.
creators.role_zh: 代码与文化研究者、作家
creators.bio_zh: 德国作家与研究者，研究文学、计算与媒介文化，长期任职于鹿特丹 Piet Zwart Institute 和 Willem de Kooning 学院。
creators.why_zh: 他追溯了“可执行指令”的观念：从咒语和组合诗歌一直到软件，把乐谱与代码联系起来。

creators.name: Nicolas Bourriaud
creators.bio: French curator and writer, co-founder of the Palais de Tokyo, who named the 1990s tendency of artworks built from social encounters 'relational aesthetics'.
creators.why: He made human relations and the situations an artist sets up the recognised material of contemporary art.
creators.bio_zh: 法国策展人与作家，东京宫（Palais de Tokyo）联合创办人，把 1990 年代以社交相遇为材料的艺术倾向命名为“关系美学”。
creators.why_zh: 他让人际关系以及艺术家设定的情境成为当代艺术公认的材料。

creators.name: Claire Bishop
creators.bio: British art historian, professor at the CUNY Graduate Center, who writes on participatory art, installation and performance.
creators.why: She wrote the standard history and critique of participatory art, asking what audiences actually do and who sets the rules.
creators.bio_zh: 英国艺术史学者，任教于纽约市立大学研究生中心，研究参与式艺术、装置与表演。
creators.why_zh: 她写出了参与式艺术的标准历史与批评，追问观众实际做了什么、规则由谁设定。

creators.name: Grant Kester
creators.bio: American art historian at the University of California, San Diego, who studies collaborative and socially engaged art.
creators.why: He described 'dialogical art', where the work is a structured conversation between an artist and a community.
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术史学者，任教于加州大学圣地亚哥分校，研究协作式与社会介入式艺术。
creators.why_zh: 他提出“对话性艺术”：作品是艺术家与社区之间一场有结构的对话。

creators.name: Hans Ulrich Obrist
creators.bio: Swiss curator, artistic director of the Serpentine Galleries in London, who started the instruction-based exhibition do it in 1993.
creators.why: do it turned the exhibition into a set of artists' instructions that any institution or reader can carry out.
creators.bio_zh: 瑞士策展人，伦敦蛇形画廊艺术总监，1993 年发起以指令为基础的展览 do it。
creators.why_zh: do it 把展览变成一组艺术家指令，任何机构或读者都能执行。

creators.name: Ruth Catlow
creators.role: Artist, curator and co-founder of Furtherfield
creators.bio: British artist and curator, co-founder and co-artistic director of Furtherfield, and a leading researcher of blockchain, DAOs and the arts.
creators.why: Her edited books set the agenda for artists treating blockchains and DAOs as tools to redesign how art is owned and governed.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、策展人，Furtherfield 联合创办人
creators.bio_zh: 英国艺术家与策展人，Furtherfield 联合创办人及联合艺术总监，是区块链、DAO 与艺术领域的重要研究者。
creators.why_zh: 她主编的书为“艺术家用区块链和 DAO 重新设计艺术的所有与治理”设定了议程。

creators.name: Marc Garrett
creators.role: Artist, writer and co-founder of Furtherfield
creators.bio: British artist, writer and curator who co-founded the London art and technology organisation Furtherfield with Ruth Catlow in 1996.
creators.why: He co-edited the first book on what blockchains mean for art production and distribution.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、作家，Furtherfield 联合创办人
creators.bio_zh: 英国艺术家、作家与策展人，1996 年与 Ruth Catlow 共同创办伦敦艺术与技术机构 Furtherfield。
creators.why_zh: 他参与主编了第一本讨论区块链对艺术生产与传播意味着什么的书。

creators.name: Penny Rafferty
creators.bio: Writer and researcher working on art, blockchain and DAOs, and co-editor of Radical Friends with Ruth Catlow.
creators.why: She helped shift the art-and-blockchain debate from NFTs toward DAOs as a way for artists to organise.
creators.bio_zh: 研究艺术、区块链与 DAO 的作家和研究者，与 Ruth Catlow 共同主编《Radical Friends》。
creators.why_zh: 她推动艺术与区块链的讨论从 NFT 转向 DAO，把 DAO 视为艺术家自我组织的方式。

creators.name: Rhea Myers
creators.bio: Artist, hacker and writer who has made blockchain artworks since 2011, including early smart-contract works and conceptual pieces about value and ownership.
creators.why: One of the first artists to treat smart contracts as a conceptual-art medium, and a sharp critic of crypto culture.
creators.bio_zh: 艺术家、黑客与作家，自 2011 年起创作区块链艺术，包括早期的智能合约作品以及关于价值与所有权的观念作品。
creators.why_zh: 她是最早把智能合约当作观念艺术媒介的艺术家之一，也是加密文化的尖锐批评者。

creators.name: Kei Kreutler
creators.role: Artist, writer and co-founder of Gnosis Guild
creators.bio: Artist and writer working on decentralized organisations, co-founder of Gnosis Guild, which builds open tools for DAOs.
creators.why: Her essay places DAOs in a longer history of cooperatives and game guilds, giving art DAOs a lineage beyond crypto.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、作家，Gnosis Guild 联合创办人
creators.bio_zh: 研究去中心化组织的艺术家与作家，Gnosis Guild 联合创办人，该团队为 DAO 开发开源工具。
creators.why_zh: 她的文章把 DAO 放进合作社和游戏公会的长历史里，为艺术 DAO 提供了加密之外的谱系。

creators.name: Primavera De Filippi
creators.bio: Researcher at the CNRS in Paris and faculty associate at Harvard's Berkman Klein Center, who studies blockchain governance and makes artworks such as the blockchain-based flower Plantoid.
creators.why: She works on both sides of protocol art: the law of self-executing code and artworks that own and reproduce themselves.
creators.bio_zh: 巴黎法国国家科学研究中心（CNRS）研究员、哈佛 Berkman Klein 中心研究员，研究区块链治理，并创作了基于区块链的机械花 Plantoid 等作品。
creators.why_zh: 她同时处在协议艺术的两端：研究自动执行代码的法律，也创作能拥有并繁殖自己的作品。

creators.name: Aaron Wright
creators.bio: American law professor at Cardozo School of Law, where he directs the Tech Startup Clinic, and co-author of Blockchain and the Law.
creators.why: He helped define how smart contracts and DAOs relate to legal rules, the frame artists now use for contract-based works.
creators.bio_zh: 美国法学教授，任教于 Cardozo 法学院并主持其科技创业法律诊所，《Blockchain and the Law》合著者。
creators.why_zh: 他帮助界定智能合约与 DAO 同法律规则的关系，这正是艺术家创作合约作品时所依托的框架。

creators.name: Amy Whitaker
creators.bio: American writer and professor at New York University's Steinhardt School who studies art markets, artists' equity and blockchain.
creators.why: She mapped the early uses of blockchain in the arts and proposed shared-equity models that give artists a stake in resales.
creators.bio_zh: 美国作家，纽约大学 Steinhardt 学院教授，研究艺术市场、艺术家权益与区块链。
creators.why_zh: 她梳理了区块链在艺术中的早期用途，并提出让艺术家分享转售收益的共同权益模式。

creators.name: Summer of Protocols
creators.bio: Research programme commissioned by the Ethereum Foundation in late 2022 that brought researchers, artists and engineers together to study protocols across fields; it ran seasons from 2023 to 2025.
creators.why: It built a shared vocabulary for protocols as a designable, cultural form, the ground on which 'protocolized' art and design now stand.
creators.bio_zh: 由以太坊基金会于 2022 年底委托发起的研究计划，把研究者、艺术家和工程师聚在一起跨领域研究协议，2023 至 2025 年每年举办一季。
creators.why_zh: 它建立了一套把协议视为可设计的文化形式的共同词汇，是“协议化”艺术与设计的理论基础。

creators.name: Venkatesh Rao
creators.bio: Indian-American writer, founder of the blog Ribbonfarm, and a director of the Summer of Protocols research programme.
creators.why: He led the effort to treat protocols as a general subject of study, from traffic rules to blockchains.
creators.bio_zh: 印度裔美国作家，博客 Ribbonfarm 创办人，Summer of Protocols 研究计划的负责人之一。
creators.why_zh: 他主导把协议作为一个普遍研究对象来看待，从交通规则到区块链。

creators.name: Jacob Horne
creators.bio: American entrepreneur and co-founder of Zora, an onchain protocol and platform for minting and collecting media.
creators.why: His essay Hyperstructures named the idea of protocols that run without their makers, a design goal for many onchain art systems.
creators.bio_zh: 美国创业者，Zora 联合创办人；Zora 是一个用于铸造和收藏媒体的链上协议与平台。
creators.why_zh: 他的文章《Hyperstructures》提出了“脱离创造者也能持续运行的协议”这一概念，成为许多链上艺术系统的设计目标。

creators.name: Malte Rauch
creators.bio: Curator and writer on blockchain art who has worked with Bright Moments and the Verse platform, and wrote the essay for the contract show World Computer Sculpture Garden.
creators.why: His essay gives one of the clearest definitions of protocol art as art concerned with the rules that precede and define a computing environment.
creators.bio_zh: 研究区块链艺术的策展人与作家，曾与 Bright Moments 和 Verse 平台合作，为合约展览 World Computer Sculpture Garden 撰写文章。
creators.why_zh: 他的文章对协议艺术给出了最清晰的定义之一：关注先于并界定计算环境之规则的艺术。

creators.name: Botao Amber Hu
creators.role: Designer and researcher, Reality Design Lab
creators.bio: Designer and HCI researcher who leads Reality Design Lab and publishes on protocol art, speculative design, mixed reality and decentralized AI.
creators.why: Author of the first peer-reviewed study that defines protocol art through a close reading of Pak's smart-contract works.
creators.role_zh: 设计师、研究者，Reality Design Lab
creators.bio_zh: 设计师与人机交互研究者，主持 Reality Design Lab，发表关于协议艺术、思辨设计、混合现实与去中心化 AI 的研究。
creators.why_zh: 他撰写了第一篇通过细读 Pak 的智能合约作品来界定协议艺术的同行评审论文。

creators.name: Mat Dryhurst
creators.bio: Artist and researcher who works with Holly Herndon on AI and voice projects such as Holly+, and co-founded Spawning, which builds consent tools for AI training data.
creators.why: He argues that artists should design protocols directly, as 'executable critique', rather than make work inside platforms.
creators.bio_zh: 艺术家与研究者，与 Holly Herndon 合作 Holly+ 等 AI 与声音项目，并联合创办 Spawning，为 AI 训练数据开发授权同意工具。
creators.why_zh: 他主张艺术家应当直接设计协议，作为“可执行的批判”，而不是在平台内部做作品。

creators.name: Vera List Center for Art and Politics
creators.role: Research center at The New School
creators.bio: Research and public programme centre at The New School in New York that works on the relation between art and politics through seasonal focus themes.
creators.why: Its multi-year focus theme and book As for Protocols treat protocols as shared social forms that artists can rewrite.
creators.bio_zh: 纽约新学院（The New School）下属的研究与公共项目中心，以分季主题研究艺术与政治的关系。
creators.why_zh: 它多年的焦点主题和《As for Protocols》一书把协议视为艺术家可以重写的共享社会形式。

works.title: Paragraphs on Conceptual Art
works.description: Essay published in the Summer 1967 issue of Artforum in which LeWitt defines Conceptual art: the idea is the most important part of the work, and its execution follows a plan fixed in advance.
works.description_zh: 1967 年夏季号《Artforum》上发表的文章。LeWitt 在其中界定观念艺术：观念是作品最重要的部分，执行只是按照事先确定的计划进行。
works.idea_en: Write the plan first; once it exists, the idea becomes a machine that makes the art.
works.idea_zh: 先写下计划；计划一旦存在，观念就成了制造艺术的机器。
works.protocol: All planning and decisions are made beforehand and 'the execution is a perfunctory affair'; the artist fixes a premise and a system, and anyone following it produces the work without new aesthetic choices.
works.protocol_zh: 所有计划和决定都事先完成，“执行只是例行公事”；艺术家确定前提和系统，任何人照做都能完成作品，无需再做审美选择。
works.collective: The text became the working manifesto for instruction-based practice: LeWitt's own wall drawings are still executed by drafters and museum teams from his written instructions, and later instruction, score and code-based artists cite it as a starting point.
works.collective_zh: 这篇文章成为指令式创作的工作宣言：LeWitt 自己的墙绘至今仍由绘图员和博物馆团队根据他的书面指令执行，后来的指令、乐谱与代码艺术家也常以它为起点。

paper.title: Paragraphs on Conceptual Art

works.title: Sentences on Conceptual Art
works.description: Thirty-five numbered statements first printed in the magazine 0 to 9 (no. 5, January 1969) and then in the first issue of Art-Language (May 1969), extending LeWitt's argument that ideas alone can be works of art.
works.description_zh: 三十五条编号语句，首先刊于杂志《0 to 9》第 5 期（1969 年 1 月），随后刊于《Art-Language》创刊号（1969 年 5 月），延续了 LeWitt“观念本身即可成为艺术作品”的论点。
works.idea_en: Once the process is set, let it run: follow the rules even when the result surprises you.
works.idea_zh: 过程一旦设定就让它运行：即使结果出乎意料，也按规则走下去。
works.protocol: The sentences state that the artist should not change the idea mid-course, that the process is mechanical once begun, and that 'the idea becomes a machine that makes the art'; perception of the work is left to each viewer.
works.protocol_zh: 这些语句规定：艺术家不应在中途改变观念；过程一旦开始便是机械的；“观念成为制造艺术的机器”；对作品的感知则留给每位观者。
works.collective: Reprinted in most Conceptual art anthologies, the sentences are read as a rulebook by artists who write systems for others to run, from wall-drawing assistants to generative and smart-contract artists.
works.collective_zh: 这组语句被大多数观念艺术文集收录，被那些为他人编写可执行系统的艺术家当作规则手册来读：从墙绘助手到生成艺术和智能合约艺术家。

paper.title: Sentences on Conceptual Art

works.title: Systems Esthetics
works.description: Essay in Artforum (September 1968) arguing that art was shifting from making objects to organising systems: relations between people, materials, information and institutions over time.
works.description_zh: 发表于《Artforum》（1968 年 9 月）的文章，认为艺术正从制造物体转向组织系统：人、材料、信息与机构之间随时间变化的关系。
works.idea_en: The artwork is not the object but the system of relations it sets in motion.
works.idea_zh: 作品不是物体，而是它所启动的关系系统。
works.protocol: Burnham borrows from systems theory and cybernetics: a work is a set of components and the rules of their interaction, and the artist designs those relations instead of a finished form.
works.protocol_zh: Burnham 借用系统论和控制论：作品是一组组成部分及其相互作用的规则，艺术家设计的是这些关系，而不是一个完成的形式。
works.collective: The essay gave critics and artists (Hans Haacke among them) a language for process, ecological and information-based work, and is now a standard reference for software, network and protocol art.
works.collective_zh: 这篇文章为评论家和艺术家（包括 Hans Haacke）提供了讨论过程、生态与信息类作品的语言，如今是软件、网络与协议艺术的标准参考文献。

paper.title: Systems Esthetics

works.title: Software: Information Technology: Its New Meaning for Art
works.description: Exhibition and catalogue curated by Burnham at the Jewish Museum, New York (16 September – 8 November 1970), that showed conceptual artists and computer systems side by side, treating 'software' as instructions carried out by machines or by visitors.
works.description_zh: Burnham 在纽约犹太博物馆策划的展览及其画册（1970 年 9 月 16 日至 11 月 8 日），把观念艺术家与计算机系统并置，把“软件”理解为由机器或观众执行的指令。
works.idea_en: An exhibition can be a program: instructions that visitors and machines execute together.
works.idea_zh: 展览本身可以是一段程序：由观众和机器共同执行的指令。
works.protocol: Works were framed as 'software': sets of instructions written by the artist and run by a computer or by the public, such as Hans Haacke's Visitor's Profile, which tabulated visitors' answers to a questionnaire, and Ted Nelson's hypertext catalogue Labyrinth.
works.protocol_zh: 作品被当作“软件”来呈现：由艺术家写下、由计算机或公众执行的指令组，例如 Hans Haacke 的 Visitor's Profile（统计观众填写的问卷）和 Ted Nelson 的超文本目录 Labyrinth。
works.collective: Visitors' answers and actions supplied the content of several works; the show, which also travelled to the Smithsonian, is remembered as the first major US museum exhibition to bring the computer into the gallery.
works.collective_zh: 观众的回答和操作构成了多件作品的内容；该展随后巡回至史密森尼学会，被视为美国第一个把计算机带进展厅的大型博物馆展览。

paper.venue: The Jewish Museum, New York, 1970 (exhibition catalogue)
paper.title: Software: Information Technology: Its New Meaning for Art

works.title: Is There Love in the Telematic Embrace?
works.description: Essay in Art Journal (Autumn 1990) in which Ascott describes telematic art: works made by many participants linked through computer networks, with meaning produced in their exchanges.
works.description_zh: 发表于《Art Journal》（1990 年秋季号）的文章。Ascott 在其中描述远程通信艺术：由通过计算机网络相连的众多参与者共同完成、意义在其交流中产生的作品。
works.idea_en: On a network, authorship is distributed: the artist sets up the link, the participants make the work.
works.idea_zh: 在网络上，作者身份是分布式的：艺术家搭建连接，参与者完成作品。
works.protocol: The artist provides a networked context and a few rules for contribution; participants at distant nodes add, transform and pass on material, and no single author controls the result.
works.protocol_zh: 艺术家提供一个网络化的情境和少量参与规则；远方节点上的参与者添加、改写并传递素材，没有哪个单一作者能控制结果。
works.collective: The essay draws on Ascott's own networked projects, such as La Plissure du Texte (1983), in which participants in several cities wrote a fairy tale together; it became a founding text for telematic and net art and titles his collected writings, Telematic Embrace (2003).
works.collective_zh: 文章基于 Ascott 自己的网络项目，例如 La Plissure du Texte（1983），多个城市的参与者在其中共同写作一则童话；它成为远程通信艺术与网络艺术的奠基文本，也成为他文集《Telematic Embrace》（2003）的书名。

paper.title: Is There Love in the Telematic Embrace?

works.title: Conceptual Art 1962–1969: From the Aesthetic of Administration to the Critique of Institutions
works.description: Essay in October (Winter 1990) that reads Conceptual art through its use of administrative forms: certificates, statements, lists, legal contracts and instructions.
works.description_zh: 发表于《October》（1990 年冬季号）的文章，从行政形式的角度解读观念艺术：证书、声明、清单、法律契约与指令。
works.idea_en: Paperwork is a medium: certificates and contracts can carry the whole work.
works.idea_zh: 文书本身就是媒介：证书和契约可以承载整件作品。
works.protocol: Buchloh argues that artists such as LeWitt, Kosuth, Weiner and Haacke replaced craft with the procedures of bureaucracy, so that the work consists of rules, documents and institutional relations.
works.protocol_zh: Buchloh 认为 LeWitt、Kosuth、Weiner 和 Haacke 等艺术家以官僚程序取代了手艺，作品因此由规则、文件和机构关系构成。
works.collective: The essay framed later readings of certificates, receipts and artist contracts as art, the lineage that curators and writers now connect to smart-contract art.
works.collective_zh: 这篇文章影响了后来把证书、收据和艺术家契约视为艺术的解读，策展人和作者如今把这一脉络与智能合约艺术联系起来。

paper.title: Conceptual Art 1962–1969: From the Aesthetic of Administration to the Critique of Institutions

works.title: Protocol: How Control Exists after Decentralization
works.description: Book (MIT Press, 2004) arguing that the internet is organised not by freedom but by protocols such as TCP/IP and DNS, which distribute control into technical standards; it also discusses net art and hacking as practices that work inside protocol.
works.description_zh: 一本书（MIT Press，2004），认为互联网并非由自由组织，而是由 TCP/IP、DNS 等协议组织，控制被分散到技术标准之中；书中也讨论了在协议内部工作的网络艺术与黑客实践。
works.idea_en: Protocol is how control works when there is no centre: design the protocol and you design the behaviour.
works.idea_zh: 协议是没有中心时控制的运作方式：设计协议，就是设计行为。
works.protocol: Galloway defines protocol as a set of voluntary technical rules that every node must follow to connect; its power lies in making behaviour standard while leaving each node apparently free.
works.protocol_zh: Galloway 把协议定义为每个节点为了连接都必须遵守的一组自愿技术规则；它的力量在于让行为标准化，同时让每个节点看起来是自由的。
works.collective: The book became the main theory text for net art, tactical media and later crypto and protocol art, and is cited by artists who treat standards and smart contracts as their medium.
works.collective_zh: 这本书成为网络艺术、战术媒体以及后来加密与协议艺术的主要理论文本，被把标准和智能合约当作媒介的艺术家广泛引用。

paper.title: Protocol: How Control Exists after Decentralization

works.title: The Exploit: A Theory of Networks
works.description: Book (University of Minnesota Press, 2007) arguing that networks create their own forms of control, both centralised and dispersed, and that resistance must work through 'exploits': holes found inside the protocol itself.
works.description_zh: 一本书（明尼苏达大学出版社，2007），认为网络会产生自身特有的控制形式，既集中又分散；抵抗必须通过“漏洞利用”进行，也就是在协议内部找到的缺口。
works.idea_en: To change a network, use its own rules against it.
works.idea_zh: 要改变一个网络，就用它自己的规则反过来对付它。
works.protocol: The authors describe networks as topologies governed by protocol, and the exploit as a practice that follows the rules exactly while turning them to unintended ends.
works.protocol_zh: 作者把网络描述为由协议支配的拓扑结构，而“漏洞利用”是一种严格遵守规则、却把规则引向意外用途的实践。
works.collective: The book gave hacktivists, tactical-media groups and software artists a vocabulary for working inside network protocols rather than outside them.
works.collective_zh: 这本书为黑客行动者、战术媒体团体和软件艺术家提供了一套在网络协议内部、而非外部工作的词汇。

paper.venue: University of Minnesota Press, Electronic Mediations 21, 2007
paper.title: The Exploit: A Theory of Networks

works.title: Words Made Flesh: Code, Culture, Imagination
works.description: Book-length essay written at the Piet Zwart Institute in Rotterdam and published online in 2005, tracing the idea of executable language from magic and combinatory poetry to Fluxus scores and computer code.
works.description_zh: 在鹿特丹 Piet Zwart Institute 写成、2005 年在网上发表的长篇论文，追溯“可执行语言”的观念：从魔法和组合诗歌到激浪派乐谱和计算机代码。
works.idea_en: A score, a spell and a program share one property: words that make things happen when executed.
works.idea_zh: 乐谱、咒语和程序有一个共同点：它们是被执行时会让事情发生的文字。
works.protocol: Cramer shows that instructions have a long cultural history outside computing, and that the same text can be read as description or run as action, by people or by machines.
works.protocol_zh: Cramer 指出，指令在计算之外有很长的文化历史；同一段文本既可以被当作描述来读，也可以被人或机器当作行动来执行。
works.collective: Distributed free online and through the Internet Archive, the text became a common reference in software-art and code-poetry teaching.
works.collective_zh: 该文本通过网络和互联网档案馆免费流通，成为软件艺术和代码诗歌教学中常用的参考文献。

paper.title: Words Made Flesh: Code, Culture, Imagination

works.title: Relational Aesthetics
works.description: Book first published in French as Esthétique relationnelle (Les presses du réel, 1998; English 2002) that describes 1990s art whose material is human relations: shared meals, meetings, services and temporary social spaces.
works.description_zh: 一本书，法文原版《Esthétique relationnelle》由 Les presses du réel 于 1998 年出版（英文版 2002 年），描述 1990 年代以人际关系为材料的艺术：共餐、聚会、服务和临时社交空间。
works.idea_en: The artwork can be a situation: a set of conditions under which people meet and interact.
works.idea_zh: 作品可以是一个情境：一组让人们相遇和互动的条件。
works.protocol: Bourriaud describes artworks as 'social interstices': the artist sets up a situation with loose rules of use, and visitors complete it by how they gather, eat, talk or exchange.
works.protocol_zh: Bourriaud 把作品描述为“社会间隙”：艺术家设定一个带有宽松使用规则的情境，观众通过聚集、进食、交谈或交换的方式完成它。
works.collective: The book named a generation (Rirkrit Tiravanija, Liam Gillick, Philippe Parreno and others) and became one of the most cited and most debated texts on participatory art.
works.collective_zh: 这本书命名了一代艺术家（Rirkrit Tiravanija、Liam Gillick、Philippe Parreno 等），成为参与式艺术领域被引用和争论最多的文本之一。

paper.title: Esthétique relationnelle / Relational Aesthetics

works.title: Participation
works.description: Anthology edited by Bishop (Whitechapel Gallery and MIT Press, Documents of Contemporary Art, 2006) that collects theory, artists' statements and curatorial debates on art that makes spectators into participants.
works.description_zh: Bishop 主编的文集（白教堂画廊与 MIT Press 合作的“当代艺术文献”丛书，2006），收录关于“让观众成为参与者”之艺术的理论、艺术家文本与策展辩论。
works.idea_en: Participation has a history and a theory: read the rules artists wrote for audiences side by side.
works.idea_zh: 参与有它的历史和理论：把艺术家为观众写下的规则放在一起读。
works.protocol: The book gathers texts in which artists define what participants may do, from Lygia Clark, Hélio Oiticica and Joseph Beuys to Thomas Hirschhorn and Rirkrit Tiravanija, next to theory by Eco, Barthes, Rancière and Guattari.
works.protocol_zh: 书中汇集了艺术家界定参与者可以做什么的文本，从 Lygia Clark、Hélio Oiticica、Joseph Beuys 到 Thomas Hirschhorn、Rirkrit Tiravanija，并与 Eco、Barthes、Rancière、Guattari 的理论并置。
works.collective: It became a standard course reader on participatory art and included the first English translation of Rancière's 'Problems and Transformations in Critical Art'.
works.collective_zh: 它成为参与式艺术课程的标准读本，并收录了 Rancière《批判艺术的问题与转变》的第一个英译本。

paper.title: Participation

works.title: Artificial Hells: Participatory Art and the Politics of Spectatorship
works.description: Book (Verso, 2012) that gives the first historical and theoretical overview of socially engaged participatory art, from Futurist evenings and Situationism to 1960s happenings and recent social practice.
works.description_zh: 一本书（Verso，2012），首次对社会介入式参与艺术做了历史与理论的全面梳理：从未来主义之夜、情境主义到 1960 年代偶发艺术和近年的社会实践。
works.idea_en: Judge a participatory work by the tensions its rules create, not only by how nice the collaboration feels.
works.idea_zh: 评价参与式作品，要看它的规则制造了怎样的张力，而不只看合作是否愉快。
works.protocol: Bishop analyses how artists 'delegate' performance and set rules for participants, and argues against judging such work only by its ethics; the best works keep a productive discomfort between author and participants.
works.protocol_zh: Bishop 分析艺术家如何“委托”表演、为参与者设定规则，并反对只从伦理角度评价此类作品；她认为最好的作品会在作者与参与者之间保持一种有生产性的不适。
works.collective: The book shaped a decade of debate on social practice and is widely taught; its account of delegated performance applies directly to works where crowds act under an artist's rules.
works.collective_zh: 这本书塑造了此后十年关于社会实践的讨论，被广泛用于教学；其关于“委托表演”的论述，直接适用于人群在艺术家规则下行动的作品。

paper.title: Artificial Hells: Participatory Art and the Politics of Spectatorship

works.title: Conversation Pieces: Community and Communication in Modern Art
works.description: Book (University of California Press, 2004) on 'dialogical' art, where artists set up long-term exchanges with communities and the conversation itself becomes the work.
works.description_zh: 一本书（加州大学出版社，2004），讨论“对话性”艺术：艺术家与社区建立长期交流，交流本身成为作品。
works.idea_en: Design the conversation, not the object: the work is what people say and decide together.
works.idea_zh: 设计的是对话而非物件：作品就是人们共同说出和决定的内容。
works.protocol: Kester describes projects in which the artist frames a dialogue among groups that rarely meet (for example officials, workers and residents) and the outcome is decided in that exchange.
works.protocol_zh: Kester 描述了这样的项目：艺术家为很少相遇的群体（例如官员、劳动者和居民）搭建对话框架，结果在交流中决定。
works.collective: The book, reissued in an updated edition in 2013, became a key reference for collaborative and community-based art, offering an alternative to judging such work by its visual form.
works.collective_zh: 该书于 2013 年推出增订版，成为协作式与社区艺术的重要参考，提供了一种不以视觉形式评判此类作品的思路。

paper.title: Conversation Pieces: Community and Communication in Modern Art

works.title: do it: the compendium
works.description: Book (Independent Curators International and D.A.P., 2013) collecting twenty years of the do it exhibition, begun in Paris in 1993, in which artists write instructions that institutions and readers carry out.
works.description_zh: 一本书（独立策展人国际与 D.A.P.，2013），汇集始于 1993 年巴黎的展览 do it 二十年的成果：艺术家写下指令，由机构和读者执行。
works.idea_en: An exhibition can travel as a set of instructions and be remade differently each time.
works.idea_zh: 展览可以作为一组指令流动，每次都以不同方式被重新制作。
works.protocol: Each artist contributes a written instruction; any host may realise it with local means, and each realisation counts as a version of the work, not a copy.
works.protocol_zh: 每位艺术家提供一条书面指令；任何主办方都可以用本地条件实现它，每次实现都算作作品的一个版本，而不是复制品。
works.collective: The compendium prints instructions by 250 artists, 84 of them newly published for the 20th anniversary, together with essays and documentation of past iterations staged by institutions around the world.
works.collective_zh: 该书收录了 250 位艺术家的指令，其中 84 条为二十周年新发表，另附文章以及世界各地机构历次实施的记录。

paper.title: do it: the compendium

works.title: Artists Re:Thinking the Blockchain
works.description: Anthology edited by Ruth Catlow, Marc Garrett, Nathan Jones and Sam Skinner (Torque Editions with Furtherfield and FACT, 2017), the first book on what blockchain technologies mean for art production and distribution.
works.description_zh: 由 Ruth Catlow、Marc Garrett、Nathan Jones 和 Sam Skinner 主编的文集（Torque Editions 联合 Furtherfield 与 FACT，2017），是第一本讨论区块链技术对艺术生产与传播意味着什么的书。
works.idea_en: Ask what a blockchain could do for art beyond selling it: new rules for value, ownership and cooperation.
works.idea_zh: 问问区块链除了卖艺术还能做什么：为价值、所有权与合作制定新规则。
works.protocol: The editors commissioned artists and researchers over a 12-month process to test blockchains as a medium; the book's companion interface, Finbook, let readers and bots trade on the value of its chapters.
works.protocol_zh: 编者用 12 个月时间委托艺术家和研究者，把区块链当作媒介来测试；配套界面 Finbook 让读者和机器人对书中各章的价值进行交易。
works.collective: Contributors included Rhea Myers, Primavera De Filippi and Jaya Klara Brekke; a free digital edition was launched at Transmediale in February 2018, and the book seeded Furtherfield's DAO research that led to Radical Friends.
works.collective_zh: 撰稿人包括 Rhea Myers、Primavera De Filippi 和 Jaya Klara Brekke；免费电子版于 2018 年 2 月在 Transmediale 发布，这本书也开启了 Furtherfield 此后通向《Radical Friends》的 DAO 研究。

paper.title: Artists Re:Thinking the Blockchain

works.title: Radical Friends: Decentralised Autonomous Organisations and the Arts
works.description: Book edited by Ruth Catlow and Penny Rafferty (Torque Editions, 2022) with essays, interviews, exercises and prototypes on DAOs as tools for artists to encode rules, relations and values into shared ventures.
works.description_zh: Ruth Catlow 与 Penny Rafferty 主编的书（Torque Editions，2022），以文章、访谈、练习和原型讨论 DAO 如何让艺术家把规则、关系与价值写进共同事业。
works.idea_en: The most radical blockchain tool for art may be the organisation, not the token.
works.idea_zh: 对艺术来说，最激进的区块链工具也许是组织，而不是代币。
works.protocol: The book treats a DAO as a rule set that peers write together and run on a blockchain: who can join, how decisions are made, how money flows. It includes exercises for groups to draft their own.
works.protocol_zh: 书中把 DAO 看作同伴们共同编写、运行在区块链上的一组规则：谁可以加入、如何决策、资金如何流动；并附有供团体起草自己规则的练习。
works.collective: It collects more than five years of research by the editors and contributors such as Primavera De Filippi, Ramon Amaro, Mitchell F. Chan and eeefff, and refocused attention from NFTs toward collective organisation in the arts.
works.collective_zh: 它汇集了编者及 Primavera De Filippi、Ramon Amaro、Mitchell F. Chan、eeefff 等撰稿人五年多的研究，把关注点从 NFT 转向艺术中的集体组织。

paper.title: Radical Friends: Decentralised Autonomous Organisations and the Arts

works.title: Proof of Work: Blockchain Provocations 2011–2021
works.description: Book (Urbanomic / Art Editions, 2023) collecting Myers's blockchain artworks from 2011 to 2021 with annotations, alongside her essays, reviews and fiction on crypto culture and art.
works.description_zh: 一本书（Urbanomic / Art Editions，2023），收录 Myers 2011 至 2021 年的区块链作品及注释，以及她关于加密文化与艺术的文章、评论和小说。
works.idea_en: Use the tropes of Conceptual art to ask what a blockchain reveals about value and ownership.
works.idea_zh: 借用观念艺术的套路，追问区块链揭示了关于价值与所有权的什么。
works.protocol: Many works in the book are small smart contracts or token schemes with a conceptual twist, whose rules collectors and the network carry out; the texts explain each rule and its art-historical reference.
works.protocol_zh: 书中许多作品是带有观念转折的小型智能合约或代币机制，其规则由藏家和网络执行；文字部分解释每条规则及其艺术史参照。
works.collective: The book documents a decade of work that anticipated the NFT boom, and was also issued as an NFT special edition by Urbanomic.
works.collective_zh: 这本书记录了先于 NFT 热潮的十年创作，Urbanomic 还发行了它的 NFT 特别版。

paper.title: Proof of Work: Blockchain Provocations 2011–2021

works.title: A Prehistory of DAOs
works.description: Essay published by Gnosis Guild in July 2021, subtitled 'Cooperatives, gaming guilds, and the networks to come', that traces DAOs back to the cooperative movement and online game guilds.
works.description_zh: Gnosis Guild 于 2021 年 7 月发表的文章，副标题为“合作社、游戏公会与即将到来的网络”，把 DAO 的源头追溯到合作社运动和网络游戏公会。
works.idea_en: DAOs are not new: they are cooperatives and guilds with their rules written in code.
works.idea_zh: DAO 并不新：它们是把规则写进代码的合作社和公会。
works.protocol: Kreutler reads DAOs as organisations where a software protocol sets the operating rules, 'placing automation at its center and humans at its edges', and compares them to the Rochdale cooperative principles of 1844 and guilds' loot-sharing systems such as Dragon Kill Points.
works.protocol_zh: Kreutler 把 DAO 理解为由软件协议设定运行规则的组织，“把自动化置于中心、把人置于边缘”，并将其与 1844 年罗奇代尔合作社原则以及“屠龙点数”（DKP）等公会战利品分配制度相比较。
works.collective: The essay and its LisCon talk were widely shared in the 2021 DAO wave and are often cited by art DAOs and researchers looking for a history longer than Ethereum.
works.collective_zh: 这篇文章及其在 LisCon 的演讲在 2021 年 DAO 热潮中被广泛传播，常被寻找比以太坊更长历史的艺术 DAO 和研究者引用。

paper.title: A Prehistory of DAOs: Cooperatives, gaming guilds, and the networks to come

works.title: Blockchain and the Law: The Rule of Code
works.description: Book (Harvard University Press, 2018) on how blockchains let rules be written as self-executing code, a new order the authors call 'lex cryptographia', with chapters on smart contracts, DAOs and autonomous systems.
works.description_zh: 一本书（哈佛大学出版社，2018），讨论区块链如何让规则以自动执行的代码形式存在，作者称之为“加密法”（lex cryptographia），各章涉及智能合约、DAO 与自治系统。
works.idea_en: When rules run as code, the code becomes a kind of law: design it as carefully as a constitution.
works.idea_zh: 当规则以代码运行，代码就成了一种法律：要像设计宪法一样谨慎地设计它。
works.protocol: The authors explain how smart contracts enforce agreements without courts and how DAOs and autonomous agents can hold assets and act under code, and set out where this collides with existing law.
works.protocol_zh: 作者解释智能合约如何在没有法院的情况下执行协议，DAO 与自治代理如何在代码之下持有资产和行动，并指出这些与现行法律的冲突之处。
works.collective: The book became a standard reference for law and governance of blockchain systems; De Filippi applies the same ideas in artworks such as Plantoid and in the Radical Friends anthology.
works.collective_zh: 这本书成为区块链系统法律与治理的标准参考；De Filippi 也把同样的想法用于 Plantoid 等作品以及《Radical Friends》文集中。

paper.title: Blockchain and the Law: The Rule of Code

works.title: Art and Blockchain: A Primer, History, and Taxonomy of Blockchain Use Cases in the Arts
works.description: Peer-reviewed article in Artivate (vol. 8, no. 2, 2019) that explains blockchain for arts readers, gives a history of its uses in art and sorts them into a taxonomy.
works.description_zh: 发表于《Artivate》（第 8 卷第 2 期，2019）的同行评审论文，为艺术领域读者讲解区块链，梳理其在艺术中的应用历史，并建立分类。
works.idea_en: Blockchain can change who holds a stake in an artwork, not only how it is sold.
works.idea_zh: 区块链改变的不只是作品如何出售，还有谁能在作品中持有份额。
works.protocol: Whitaker classifies use cases (provenance registries, fractional ownership, resale royalties, new funding structures) and discusses how they blur the line between for-profit and nonprofit support for art.
works.protocol_zh: Whitaker 对应用场景进行分类（来源登记、碎片化所有权、转售版税、新的资助结构），并讨论它们如何模糊营利与非营利艺术资助之间的界线。
works.collective: Published before the 2021 NFT boom, the article became an early scholarly reference for art-market and arts-management research on tokens and shared ownership.
works.collective_zh: 这篇论文发表于 2021 年 NFT 热潮之前，成为艺术市场与艺术管理领域研究代币和共享所有权的早期学术参考。

paper.venue: Artivate: A Journal of Entrepreneurship in the Arts 8, no. 2 (2019), pp. 21–46
paper.title: Art and Blockchain: A Primer, History, and Taxonomy of Blockchain Use Cases in the Arts

works.title: Summer of Protocols
works.description: Research programme commissioned by the Ethereum Foundation that ran seasons in 2023, 2024 and 2025, funding researchers, artists and engineers to study protocols across fields from blockchains to traffic, safety and diplomacy.
works.description_zh: 由以太坊基金会委托的研究计划，在 2023、2024、2025 年各举办一季，资助研究者、艺术家和工程师跨领域研究协议，从区块链到交通、安全与外交。
works.idea_en: Treat protocols as a general design material that can be studied, taught and made by artists as well as engineers.
works.idea_zh: 把协议当作一种通用的设计材料：它可以被研究、被教授，也可以由艺术家和工程师共同创作。
works.protocol: Each season invited cohorts of researchers to produce essays, artworks and tools under a shared brief; outputs are published openly and discussed in a public forum and newsletter.
works.protocol_zh: 每一季邀请一批研究者在共同主题下产出文章、作品和工具；成果公开发布，并在公共论坛和通讯中讨论。
works.collective: SoP23 brought together 12 core and 18 affiliate researchers; across its seasons the programme counts 70-odd alumni and more than 100 research outputs, including the Protocol Reader, the ProtocolKit and a 358-page proto-textbook, and it continues as the Protocol Institute.
works.collective_zh: SoP23 汇集了 12 位核心研究者和 18 位附属研究者；各季累计约 70 位参与者、100 多项研究成果，包括 Protocol Reader、ProtocolKit 和一本 358 页的原型教科书；该计划之后延续为 Protocol Institute。

paper.title: About Summer of Protocols

works.title: The Unreasonable Sufficiency of Protocols
works.description: Pilot study by Venkatesh Rao, Tim Beiko, Danny Ryan, Josh Stark, Trent Van Epps and Bastian Aue, released in March 2023 to open the Summer of Protocols, that asks why simple protocols coordinate so much complex behaviour.
works.description_zh: 由 Venkatesh Rao、Tim Beiko、Danny Ryan、Josh Stark、Trent Van Epps 与 Bastian Aue 撰写的试点研究，2023 年 3 月发布，作为 Summer of Protocols 的开篇，追问为什么简单的协议能协调如此复杂的行为。
works.idea_en: A small set of codified rules can be unreasonably sufficient: it lets large, complex cooperation emerge.
works.idea_zh: 一小组成文规则可以“不合理地充分”：它能让大规模的复杂合作涌现出来。
works.protocol: The paper defines a protocol as 'a stratum of codified behavior that allows for the construction or emergence of complex coordinated behaviors at adjacent loci', and describes protocols along dimensions such as generativity, legibility, evolvability, legitimacy, play value and mortality.
works.protocol_zh: 论文把协议定义为“一层成文的行为规范，使相邻位置上复杂的协调行为得以构建或涌现”，并从生成性、可读性、可演化性、正当性、游戏价值和寿命等维度描述协议。
works.collective: The text framed the research questions for the first Summer of Protocols cohort and was revised and republished in 2024 as a reference work for the programme.
works.collective_zh: 这篇文本为第一届 Summer of Protocols 的研究者设定了研究问题，并于 2024 年修订再版，成为该计划的参考文献。

paper.title: The Unreasonable Sufficiency of Protocols

works.title: Hyperstructures
works.description: Essay published on 16 January 2022 that defines hyperstructures as 'crypto protocols that can run for free and forever, without maintenance, interruption or intermediaries'.
works.description_zh: 2022 年 1 月 16 日发表的文章，把“超结构”定义为“能够免费、永久运行，无需维护、不会中断、没有中介的加密协议”。
works.idea_en: Build the protocol so it keeps running after you leave; then others can build on it.
works.idea_zh: 把协议做成你离开后仍能运行的样子，别人才能在上面继续建造。
works.protocol: Horne lists the properties of a hyperstructure: unstoppable, free, valuable, expansive, permissionless, positive-sum and credibly neutral, running entirely onchain for as long as its chain exists.
works.protocol_zh: Horne 列出超结构的特性：不可阻止、免费、有价值、可扩展、无需许可、正和、可信中立，完全在链上运行，只要所在的链存在就一直运行。
works.collective: The term spread quickly among onchain builders and artists and shaped Zora's own protocol design; it is often used to describe artworks and platforms meant to outlive their authors.
works.collective_zh: 这个词在链上开发者和艺术家中迅速传播，也塑造了 Zora 自身的协议设计；它常被用来描述那些意在比作者存续更久的作品与平台。

paper.title: Hyperstructures

works.title: Computation in the Expanded Field
works.description: Essay written for World Computer Sculpture Garden, a 'contract show' curated by 0xfff that opened on Ethereum in November 2024, defining protocol art as art that works with the rules that precede and define a computing environment.
works.description_zh: 为 0xfff 策划、2024 年 11 月在以太坊上开幕的“合约展”World Computer Sculpture Garden 撰写的文章，把协议艺术定义为处理那些先于并界定计算环境之规则的艺术。
works.idea_en: The blockchain is not a channel for images but the material itself: a set of constraints adopted for art.
works.idea_zh: 区块链不是图像的发行渠道，而是材料本身：一组为艺术所采用的约束。
works.protocol: Rauch argues that protocol artists treat distributed computation and its permanence as their medium, writing contracts that act as autonomous works rather than minting images for a marketplace.
works.protocol_zh: Rauch 认为，协议艺术家把分布式计算及其永久性当作媒介，编写作为自治作品运行的合约，而不是为市场铸造图像。
works.collective: The essay accompanies an exhibition that exists as a smart contract with no closing date, with works by artists including Rhea Myers and Sarah Friend, and is cited in academic work on protocol art.
works.collective_zh: 这篇文章伴随一个以智能合约形式存在、没有闭幕日期的展览，参展艺术家包括 Rhea Myers 和 Sarah Friend；该文也被协议艺术的学术研究引用。

paper.title: Computation in the Expanded Field

works.title: Protocol as Poetry: A Case Study of Pak's Smart Contract-Based Protocol Art
works.description: Peer-reviewed paper (ARTECH 2025) that analyses Pak's smart-contract works, from The Fungible and Merge (2021) to Censored (2022) and Not Found (2023), and proposes seven characteristics of protocol art.
works.description_zh: 同行评审论文（ARTECH 2025），分析 Pak 的智能合约作品，从 The Fungible 和 Merge（2021）到 Censored（2022）和 Not Found（2023），并提出协议艺术的七个特征。
works.idea_en: In protocol art the smart contract is the medium and collective participation is the message.
works.idea_zh: 在协议艺术中，智能合约是媒介，集体参与是讯息。
works.protocol: The paper names seven traits: system-centric composition, autonomous governance, distributed agency and communal authorship, temporal dynamism, economy-driven engagement, poetic messages embedded in interaction rituals, and composability.
works.protocol_zh: 论文归纳出七个特征：以系统而非物件为中心的构成、自治治理、分布式能动性与共同作者身份、时间上的动态性、由经济驱动的参与、嵌入互动仪式的诗意讯息，以及可组合性。
works.collective: It is one of the first academic studies to use the term 'protocol art' (or 'protocolism') for smart-contract works and distinguishes it from conceptual, generative, participatory and performance art.
works.collective_zh: 这是最早用“协议艺术”（或“协议主义”）来指称智能合约作品的学术研究之一，并将其与观念艺术、生成艺术、参与式艺术和表演艺术区分开来。

paper.venue: ARTECH 2025, 12th International Conference on Digital and Interactive Arts
paper.title: Protocol as Poetry: A Case Study of Pak's Smart Contract-Based Protocol Art

works.title: Protocol Futuring: Speculating Second-Order Dynamics of Protocols in Sociotechnical Infrastructural Futures
works.description: CHI 2026 paper by Botao Amber Hu, Samuel Chua and Helena Rong that proposes 'protocol futuring', a design method that uses protocols as the material of speculative design, tested in a relay workshop on millennial-scale knowledge preservation.
works.description_zh: Botao Amber Hu、Samuel Chua 与 Helena Rong 发表于 CHI 2026 的论文，提出“协议未来化”：一种把协议作为思辨设计材料的设计方法，并通过一场关于千年尺度知识保存的接力工作坊加以检验。
works.idea_en: Speculate on protocols, not products: watch how rules drift when they pass between groups and generations.
works.idea_zh: 去推演协议而不是产品：观察规则在群体与世代之间传递时如何漂移。
works.protocol: In the Knowledge Futurama workshop, teams inherited partially formed protocol designs from earlier teams and had to reinterpret and extend them, a relay rule that made drift, jamming and adversarial readings visible.
works.protocol_zh: 在 Knowledge Futurama 工作坊中，各团队从前一组那里继承尚未完成的协议设计，必须重新诠释并延续它；这种接力规则让规则的漂移、卡滞与对抗性解读变得可见。
works.collective: The multi-team relay produced protocols that changed through ambiguous handovers, shifting norms and simulated crises; the paper offers the method to HCI and design researchers studying long-lived infrastructures.
works.collective_zh: 多团队接力产出的协议在含糊的交接、变化的规范和模拟危机中不断改变；论文把这一方法提供给研究长寿命基础设施的人机交互与设计研究者。

paper.title: Protocol Futuring: Speculating Second-Order Dynamics of Protocols in Sociotechnical Infrastructural Futures

works.title: Protocol Art
works.description: Lecture published by Carrier Bag in October 2025 in which Dryhurst argues that the most consequential aesthetic decisions now happen at the level of protocols, and that artists should design protocols instead of commenting on platforms.
works.description_zh: Carrier Bag 于 2025 年 10 月发布的讲座。Dryhurst 认为，如今最重要的审美决定发生在协议层面，艺术家应当设计协议，而不是评论平台。
works.idea_en: Build the protocol as 'executable critique': a rule set others can use that carries your values downstream.
works.idea_zh: 把协议当作“可执行的批判”来建造：一套别人可以使用、并把你的价值观带到下游的规则。
works.protocol: Dryhurst uses his and Holly Herndon's projects as examples: Holly+, which lets anyone use Herndon's voice model under shared rules, the opt-out tool haveibeentrained.com, and Public Diffusion, a model trained only on public-domain data.
works.protocol_zh: Dryhurst 以他和 Holly Herndon 的项目为例：让任何人都能在共同规则下使用 Herndon 声音模型的 Holly+、退出工具 haveibeentrained.com，以及只用公有领域数据训练的模型 Public Diffusion。
works.collective: The talk extends the protocol-art discussion from smart contracts to AI: the work is judged by what other people make and decide under the rules it sets.
works.collective_zh: 这场讲座把协议艺术的讨论从智能合约扩展到 AI：作品的价值取决于其他人在它设定的规则下做出和决定了什么。

paper.title: Protocol Art

works.title: As for Protocols
works.description: Open-access book edited by Re'al Christian, Carin Kuoni and Eriola Pira (Vera List Center for Art and Politics and Amherst College Press, 2025) with contributions by 24 artists, writers, scholars, musicians, architects and scientists on protocols.
works.description_zh: 由 Re'al Christian、Carin Kuoni 与 Eriola Pira 主编的开放获取图书（Vera List 艺术与政治中心与 Amherst College Press，2025），24 位艺术家、作家、学者、音乐人、建筑师和科学家撰文讨论协议。
works.idea_en: Protocols are social forms of care and relation, and artists can write more equitable ones.
works.idea_zh: 协议是关于关怀与关系的社会形式，艺术家可以写出更公平的协议。
works.protocol: The book frames protocols as 'systems of language that regulate how we relate to each other' and to technologies, and asks contributors to propose new protocols that are inclusive and equitable.
works.protocol_zh: 该书把协议理解为“规范我们如何彼此相处”以及如何与技术相处的语言系统，并邀请撰稿人提出包容而公平的新协议。
works.collective: Contributors include Raven Chacon, Carolina Caycedo, Mary Maggic, Shannon Mattern, Rasheedah Phillips, Leanne Betasamosake Simpson, Ultra-red and Underground Resistance, drawn from the Center's multi-year focus theme.
works.collective_zh: 撰稿人包括 Raven Chacon、Carolina Caycedo、Mary Maggic、Shannon Mattern、Rasheedah Phillips、Leanne Betasamosake Simpson、Ultra-red 和 Underground Resistance，来自该中心多年的焦点主题研究。

paper.venue: Vera List Center for Art and Politics / Amherst College Press, 2025
paper.title: As for Protocols
